name: LUX
summary: LUX was a low-background liquid-xenon WIMP-search experiment at SURF. Its completed observations and technology laid the foundation for its successor LZ.
detection_principle: Dual-phase xenon S1/S2 signals measure nuclear recoils; position reconstruction and electron-recoil discrimination reduce backgrounds.

sites.name: SURF
sites.location: Sanford Underground Research Facility, Lead, South Dakota
sites.site_status: Experiment site; see the phase descriptions

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: The Berkeley Lab announcement reports the final 20 months of running data. Data taking ended in May 2016.

collaboration.name: LUX Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Only verified representative institutions are listed, not a complete membership roster. See the collaboration pages and author affiliations in the references.

results.summary: The full exposure was compatible with background, yielding limits on spin-independent WIMP–nucleon scattering.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
